source.work: Node.js and npm documentation, reproducible installs
source.locator: npm ci; pnpm install --frozen-lockfile; yarn install --immutable; core CORE-INV-050
source.paraphrase: A Node.js CI install uses the committed lockfile. npm ci, pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, and yarn install --immutable refuse a drift between the manifest and the lock.

invariants.why: An unlocked install can resolve different bytes than the ones reviewed, so CI and production are not the same dependency tree.
invariants.fixHint: Bind NODE-LOCK-001 and core CORE-INV-050 to one reviewed assertion. The assertion checks that a lockfile is committed and that CI installs with npm ci, pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, or yarn install --immutable. Include a control that changes the lock without updating the install. Run pregate fitness run NODE-LOCK-001.
invariants.avoid: Fidelity: evidence. This is the Node.js evidence for core CORE-INV-050, not a second product invariant and not a shell-gate pattern. The pack does not scan workflow YAML. A green test suite does not prove the install was frozen.

source.work: Node.js and Twelve-Factor, config and secrets
source.paraphrase: .env stays untracked because .gitignore lists it, and .env.example is committed with names and no secrets so a new checkout knows which variables exist.

invariants.why: A committed .env puts secrets in history. A missing example leaves the next checkout guessing names.
invariants.fixHint: Bind NODE-ENVFILE-001 to a reviewed assertion that fails when .env is not ignored or .env.example is absent, and that fails when the example contains a live secret. Run pregate fitness run NODE-ENVFILE-001.
invariants.avoid: Fidelity: evidence. The forbidden-path primitive requested in packs/ENGINE-REQUESTS.md section 6 is not in the engine. Until it lands, a committed .env is not a syntax finding. This obligation is the stand-in and names that dependency.

source.paraphrase: The project declares a Node.js version the pack can read, and that major is a current LTS line. The same files already gate the Node.js 26 removals.

invariants.why: An unpinned tool changes under the team. A current major that is not LTS drops support on the next release train.
invariants.fixHint: Bind NODE-PIN-001 to a reviewed assertion that reads one of .nvmrc, .node-version, .tool-versions, engines.node, or volta.node, checks the major, and checks that major against the current LTS list with an explicit maxAgeMs. Run pregate fitness run NODE-PIN-001.
invariants.avoid: Fidelity: evidence. The pack already reads these pins for the Node.js 26 gate. A missing or unreadable pin such as lts/* stays unverified. Which majors are LTS is a dated fact, so the assertion owns the list. The pack does not hardcode majors.

source.locator: npm ci --ignore-scripts; pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts; package.json install lifecycle
source.paraphrase: Dependency install scripts do not run unless they are on a reviewed allowlist. The default install passes --ignore-scripts.

invariants.why: A postinstall script from a dependency runs at install time with the developer's privileges.
invariants.fixHint: Bind NODE-SCRIPTS-001 to a reviewed assertion that accepts CI installs using --ignore-scripts, or an explicit allowlist of preinstall, install, postinstall, and prepare scripts. A script that is not listed fails the assertion. Run pregate fitness run NODE-SCRIPTS-001.
invariants.avoid: Fidelity: evidence. Workflow YAML is not a pattern grammar. This is not a shell-gate rule. A package.json script name by itself is not the allowlist.

source.paraphrase: When the Node.js process does not set security headers, the edge that terminates the request sets them, and that configuration is reviewed evidence.

invariants.why: A process behind a proxy can look header-less in source while the browser still receives no framing or transport policy if the edge never set one.
invariants.fixHint: Bind NODE-EDGE-001 to a reviewed assertion that shows the edge or gateway config setting the security headers, or that shows the process sets them. Turn NODE-HEADERS-001 off when this evidence is the one you adopt. Run pregate fitness run NODE-EDGE-001.
invariants.avoid: Fidelity: evidence. The syntax proxy cannot see the edge. A comment in server code is not this evidence.

source.work: Node.js documentation, signal events and server.close
source.paraphrase: A long-running server closes its listener when it receives SIGTERM or SIGINT so in-flight requests can finish.

invariants.why: A process that exits without close drops requests that the kernel has already accepted.
invariants.fixHint: In the file that calls createServer or listen, register process.on for SIGTERM and for SIGINT, and call server.close from each handler.
invariants.avoid: Fidelity: proxy, same-file. A handler in another file is not seen. close under another name is not seen. Test files are ignored. A comment does not count.

relations.why: Express JSON and urlencoded parsers already cap bodies at 100kb. EX-LIMIT-001 is that optional explicit limit and stays off.
relations.settle: Keep EX-LIMIT-001 off unless the project wants an explicit parser limit. This proxy is the raw server timeouts plus a named limit in the listen file.

source.locator: headersTimeout, requestTimeout, keepAliveTimeout, and a request body limit
source.paraphrase: An HTTP server bounds how long headers, the request, and a keep-alive socket may live, and it bounds the request body.

invariants.why: An unbounded header read or body holds the socket and memory for as long as the client wants.
invariants.fixHint: Set server.headersTimeout, server.requestTimeout, and server.keepAliveTimeout, and name a body limit, maxBodySize, or bodyLimit in that file.
invariants.avoid: Fidelity: proxy, same-file. Express parser limits stay express/EX-LIMIT-001, which is off because the 100kb default holds. A variable merely named limit satisfies the body half. Timeouts configured in another file are not seen. Test files are ignored.

source.work: Node.js production practice, health and readiness
source.paraphrase: A server registers /health for liveness and /ready for readiness so a platform can tell a live process from one that can take traffic.

invariants.why: A platform that cannot probe those paths restarts a healthy process or sends traffic to one that is not ready.
invariants.fixHint: Register both "/health" and "/ready" in the file that calls createServer or listen.
invariants.avoid: Fidelity: proxy, same-file. /api/health and /healthz do not count. A router mounted from another file is not seen. Test files are ignored.

source.paraphrase: The process reads process.env through one schema parse at startup. Later code uses the parsed value, not a fresh raw read.

invariants.why: A scattered read accepts a missing or mistyped variable at the moment of use, which is often the first request.
invariants.fixHint: Parse process.env once with parse, safeParse, or cleanEnv in the file that needs a value, and pass the result down. Prefer one config module.
invariants.avoid: Fidelity: proxy, same-file. schema.parse(process.env) in the same file excuses every raw read there, including one the schema does not return. const raw = process.env; schema.parse(raw) is not seen. JSON.parse does not count as that schema parse, so the raw read is still reported. Test files are ignored.

relations.why: Helmet presence is an Express backlog item because the policy may live in a reverse proxy.
relations.settle: Use this proxy for a header or helmet() call in the listen file. Use NODE-EDGE-001 when the edge owns the headers, and turn this rule off there.

source.work: OWASP HTTP security response headers and Helmet
source.locator: helmet(), or Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options
source.paraphrase: A server sets a standard security-header policy in process, or the edge does and that fact is reviewed evidence.

invariants.why: Without those headers a browser will frame the response, sniff content, or skip transport rules the app thought it had.
invariants.fixHint: Call helmet() or set one of the named headers in the listen file. When the edge sets them, bind NODE-EDGE-001 and turn this rule off.
invariants.avoid: Fidelity: proxy, same-file. One header literal satisfies the proxy; it does not prove a complete policy. The edge is NODE-EDGE-001. Test files are ignored.

source.work: Node.js production practice, request ids and structured logs
source.locator: pino or winston, and requestId or x-request-id
source.paraphrase: A server log line can be tied to one request. The logger is pino or winston, and the file names a request id.

invariants.why: A text log with no request id cannot be joined to the request that failed.
invariants.fixHint: Import pino or winston, or call pino() or winston.createLogger(), and use requestId or the header x-request-id in that file.
invariants.avoid: Fidelity: proxy, same-file. The id does not have to be passed into the logger call. console.log does not count. A logger other than pino or winston is not seen. Test files are ignored.

relations.why: Express 4 drops async rejections unless they are forwarded. Express 5 forwards them. The express pack left that as a backlog item because it depends on the major.
relations.settle: Keep this proxy at warn. When an express rule for the installed major is admitted, enable that rule and turn NODE-ASYNC-001 off for those files.

relations.why: Hono handlers are async and HONO-NEXT-001 owns awaiting next() in middleware.
relations.settle: Turn NODE-ASYNC-001 off for Hono routes. Keep HONO-NEXT-001 for middleware that calls next().

source.work: Express and Node.js HTTP, async route errors
source.locator: async handlers on get, post, put, patch, delete, all, and createServer
source.paraphrase: An async route callback is wrapped by asyncHandler, catchAsync, or wrap, or its body contains try, so a rejection reaches the error path.

invariants.why: A rejected async handler that nobody catches becomes an unhandled rejection, and the client waits.
invariants.fixHint: Wrap the handler with asyncHandler, catchAsync, or wrap, or put the awaited work in try. Sync handlers are out of scope.
invariants.avoid: Fidelity: proxy, call. Express 5 and Hono forward async rejections, so this warns on a shape their runtime already handles. app.use is not a route verb here. A wrapper with another name is not seen. Test files are ignored. Empty catch stays clean-code/CC-ER-002.

source.locator: logger and console arguments named password, secret, token, apiKey, and the other credential names
source.paraphrase: A log call does not receive a value whose name is a credential. Secrets in source stay a vibe-proof rule.

invariants.why: The log line keeps the credential in the aggregator, which is a second copy of the secret.
invariants.fixHint: Log an id or a redacted field. Do not pass password, secret, token, apiKey, accessToken, or the other listed names to logger or console.
invariants.avoid: Fidelity: proxy, argument name. A binding literally named token is flagged even when it is not a credential. requestId and tokenCount are not. A string that merely says token is not. A spread of an object is not seen. Hardcoded secret literals stay vibe-proof/VP-SECRET-001.
